refined_nucleus: A thin, porous, and negatively charged nanofiber mesh is integrated around the mechanical heart valve to mimic the natural glycocalyx and reduce platelet adhesion and coagulation activation, while also incorporating a shear-resistant material and a dynamic control system to adapt to changing blood flow conditions.
new_relationship: The nanofiber mesh's ability to reduce platelet adhesion and coagulation activation is enhanced by its dynamic interaction with the blood flow, creating a self-adaptive system.
new_configuration: The nanofiber mesh is integrated with a micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) to monitor and adjust its porosity and charge in real-time, in response to changes in blood flow conditions.
new_control_rule: The MEMS system adjusts the nanofiber mesh's porosity and charge based on real-time feedback from sensors monitoring blood flow velocity, pressure, and composition.
refined_structure: The nanofiber mesh is co-located with the mechanical heart valve and secured using a biocompatible adhesive, with the MEMS system integrated into the nanofiber mesh.
refined_causal_chain: Thrombus formation on the mechanical heart valve
Nanofiber mesh reduces platelet adhesion and coagulation activation
Dynamic MEMS system adapts to changing blood flow conditions
Self-adaptive nanofiber mesh reduces platelet adhesion and coagulation activation
Reduced risk of mechanical heart valve failure
